# Drone façade cleaning. Proven in France. Ready to scale in Thailand. 

 Tethered drones replace rope access and gondolas on glass, façades and roofs. Delivered for RATP, AP-HP, Saint-Gobain and CNRS. We are selecting a strategic partner and investors for the Thai launch.

## The investment case

 A service already delivered for large French clients, a Thai building stock that gets dirty fast, and an operating model that can be transferred. Financial information is shared in a direct meeting, under NDA.

 Proven 
### Results on demanding sites
 RATP Saint-Lazare: 400 m² of glazing in one night, with intervention time divided by five according to RATP. Saint-Gobain Recherche: a first job, then a contract for two passes a year. AP-HP: 8,570 m² of hospital glazing under contract, with flights approved by the Paris Police Prefecture.

 Market 
### A large, exposed building stock
 17,126 hotels and 711,729 rooms in Thailand in H1 2024 (Department of Tourism), plus office towers, condominiums, hospitals and factories. Heat, humidity and monsoon mean frequent cleaning.

 Model 
### A transferable method
 Cleaning protocols per material, pilot training through the TELEPILOTE training centre (since 2014), a defined equipment list and method statements ready for clients.

 Compliance 
### Regulation built in
 NBTC and CAAT registration, third-party insurance of at least 1,000,000 THB and permits for urban flights. In Paris we already work under prefectoral authorisations.

 Formats open for discussion: strategic investment in the Thai activity, joint venture with a Thai group, or licence. We are looking for one strategic partner and a small number of investors who know the Thai property, hospitality or industrial market.

## What we clean

 Most buildings get dirty where people cannot easily reach: high glass, curved façades, closed courtyards, fragile roofs. That is exactly where a drone, or a well-chosen pole or platform, saves days of scaffolding.

## Why Thai buildings need a different method

 Heat, humidity and the monsoon are hard on façades. Algae grows on shaded walls, dust and traffic soot settle on glass, and buildings near the sea collect salt. Cleaning more often is the answer, but rope access teams and building gondolas are slow to set up and put people at height.

 Thailand also has a lot of buildings to look after. The Department of Tourism counted 17,126 hotels and 711,729 rooms in the first half of 2024, before counting condominiums, office towers, hospitals, malls and factories. Many of these buildings have glass atriums, curved façades or rooftop solar that standard methods struggle with.

 A tethered drone does not replace every method. It adds one: fast on large flat or curved surfaces, no anchors on the roof, nobody hanging in front of guest rooms. We combine it with poles and platforms where they work better.

 Source: Department of Tourism, H1 2024, quoted in LH Bank, Industry Outlook 2025, five-star hotel business.

## Questions we hear first

 Do you already operate in Thailand?

 Not yet. CleanAlta operates in France and Switzerland. We are preparing the Thai launch: selecting pilot sites, finding a local partner, and registering drones and pilots with the Thai authorities before any flight.

 Is drone cleaning legal in Thailand?

 Yes, within a framework. Drones must be registered with the NBTC and the CAAT, the operator needs third-party insurance of at least 1,000,000 THB, and urban flights or flights near people need specific permission. We handle all of this before a pilot job. Details on our compliance page .

 Which buildings are a good fit?

 Buildings from about four floors up with large glass or cladding surfaces, curved façades, atriums, closed courtyards, and roofs or solar arrays that are hard to reach. Hotels, condominiums, office towers, hospitals, universities and factories are typical.

 Do you use chemicals?

 On glass, no: we use heated osmosed water at low pressure, which dries without streaks. On roofs, we apply slow-acting biocide or enzymatic treatments against moss and algae, chosen for the surface and used according to the product label.

 How much does it cost?

 It depends on surface area, height, access and dirt level, so we quote after a site survey. Pilot sites get a tailored offer in exchange for allowing us to document the job.

Services 

# Building cleaning services: the right tool for each surface

 CleanAlta is not a drone company that cleans. We are a cleaning company that uses drones where they make sense, and water-fed poles or aerial platforms where they do a better job. Two service lines, one method: purified water, low pressure, and the operator on the ground.

 Service 1 

## Façade and glass cleaning

 Curtain walls, windows, glass roofs, atriums, aluminium and composite cladding, painted or stone façades. Heated osmosed water at low pressure, no detergent on glass, and a rinse that dries without streaks.

 See the façade and glass service → 

 Service 2 

## Roof and solar panel cleaning

 Moss and algae treatment on tile, slate and metal roofs, gutters and canopies, plus gentle cleaning of photovoltaic panels on carports, warehouses and factory roofs.

 See the roof and solar service → 

## Three tools, chosen per façade

 Every site visit ends with the same question: which part of this building is best done by drone, by pole, or from a platform? Most jobs use two of the three.

 Tool Where it works best Limits 

 Tethered drone under 25 kg, power and water from the ground Large glass and cladding surfaces, upper floors, curved façades, inner courtyards, roofs. No anchors, no gondola, no one in front of the windows. Wind and rain stop flights. Needs a safety perimeter on the ground and the right permits. Heavy encrusted dirt may need brushing. 

 Water-fed pole carbon pole up to 17 m Ground to fourth floor, shop fronts, glass roofs over lift shafts, canopies. Brush contact for stubborn dirt. Height. Above about 17 m the drone or platform takes over. 

 Aerial platform up to 40 m Detail work, frames and joints, places where the drone cannot fly close enough, inspection by hand. Needs ground access and space to deploy. Slower on very large surfaces. 

## Water and products

 On glass and most façades we clean with heated osmosed water. Osmosis removes the minerals that leave white marks when tap water dries, so there is nothing to wipe. Heat helps lift grease and pollution, so we do not need detergent. Our nozzles work at low pressure and the water goes onto the surface, not into the air.

 On roofs, moss and algae come back unless the roots are treated. We spray slow-acting biocide or enzymatic treatments that keep working for weeks after the job, and we choose them for the roof material and the surroundings. Products are always used according to their label.

### What we do not do

 We focus on cleaning. The Thai offer does not include drone inspection, thermography or 3D modelling. If you need those, we can point you to specialised operators.

## See the tools at work

 The tethered drone: cable and hose from the ground unit

 Inside the van: osmosis unit, heater, pump and tether station

## How a job runs

### Photos and plans
 You send photos, the address, the height and the surfaces. We say quickly whether drone cleaning makes sense.

### Site survey
 We check take-off areas, obstacles, wind exposure, water and power supply, and who uses the ground below.

### Method statement and permits
 A written plan: tools per façade, safety perimeter, timing, flight permissions and insurance.

### Cleaning
 Ground team of two or three: a pilot, a ground operator who manages the hose and the perimeter, and a pole or platform operator when needed.

### Report
 Before and after photos, surfaces cleaned, observations on the condition of the façade.

## Service questions

 Can you clean while the building is occupied?

 Yes. We work with a closed perimeter on the ground and we agree the schedule with the site. In France we clean hospitals, research centres and stations while they stay open, sometimes at night.

 How often should a façade be cleaned in Thailand?

 It depends on exposure, the surface and how the building is used. Hotels and offices often want glass cleaned several times a year. We recommend a schedule after the first job, once we have seen how fast the building gets dirty.

 What do you need on site?

 A take-off area on the ground or a roof, access to a water point, a power supply or space for our generator, and a site contact who can close access below the work zone.

Façades · Curtain walls · Glass roofs 

# Façade and glass cleaning by drone

 Heated osmosed water, low pressure, no detergent on glass. A tethered drone does the upper floors at 500 to 800 m² per hour, a water-fed pole and a platform finish what the drone cannot reach. Nobody hangs in front of your windows.

 Request a site survey 
 Become a pilot site 

 Saint-Gobain Recherche First job led to a contract for two passes a year.

## What we clean

 Glass curtain walls on office towers, hotels and condominiums

 Windows on upper floors, including where gondolas cannot run

 Glass roofs, atriums and canopies , often impossible to reach from inside

 Cladding : aluminium, composite panels, painted or coated metal

 Mineral façades : render, concrete, stone, with a protocol per material

 Closed courtyards and curved façades where a platform cannot drive in

 In France we have written cleaning protocols per support: limestone, flamed stoneware, concrete, lacquered steel. The same discipline applies in Thailand: we test a small area first and adjust temperature, distance and passes before cleaning the whole façade.

## The method, step by step

 The drone is tethered: power and water come up through a cable and hose from the ground unit. It can stay in the air as long as the job requires, and it cannot fly away.

 1 
### Purified water
 Tap water goes through reverse osmosis to remove minerals. Without minerals, water dries without spots, so there is no need to squeegee or wipe.

 2 
### Heat, low pressure
 Heated water lifts grease, soot and pollution film. Low pressure protects seals, joints and coatings. The economical nozzle puts the water on the surface, not in the air.

 3 
### Rinse and finish
 Top-down passes with overlap, then a final rinse. The pole or the platform handles frames, corners and lower levels in the same visit.

 Saint-Gobain Recherche Aubervilliers, France Drone + pole 

## A research centre with large glass façades

 The building has long bands of glazing over several floors and a glass entrance. We cleaned the upper floors by tethered drone and the lower levels and entrance by water-fed pole, with heated osmosed water and no detergent.

 The result was good enough that, after the first intervention, Saint-Gobain Recherche signed a contract for two passes a year.

 RATP Paris Saint-Lazare October 2025

## Where it fits in Thailand

 The buildings that gain most are tall, glazed and busy, where rope access or gondolas mean weeks of disruption.

### Hotels and resorts 
 Glass façades, atriums and pool-side buildings cleaned early in the morning, without workers outside guest rooms.

### Condominiums and offices 
 Curtain walls on towers where the gondola is old, booked, or missing on part of the façade.

### Hospitals and universities 
 Sites that stay open: we work with a perimeter and a schedule agreed with the facility team.

### Malls and public buildings
 Glass roofs, canopies and entrance halls that nobody can reach from inside.

## Façade cleaning questions

 How fast is drone façade cleaning?

 Between 500 and 800 m² per hour on suitable surfaces, depending on how dirty the façade is, the method and the protocol. Set-up, perimeter and finishing by pole come on top.

 Will it leave streaks on the windows?

 Not with osmosed water. Streaks come from minerals in tap water and from detergent residues. We use neither on glass.

 Can the drone damage the façade?

 The drone does not touch the building. It sprays from a short distance at low pressure. We test a small area first on sensitive materials and adjust the protocol.

 What about wind and monsoon rain?

 We do not fly in strong wind or rain. In Thailand we plan jobs in the dry season where possible and keep flexible dates during the monsoon.

Roofs · Moss & algae · Solar panels 

# Roof and solar panel cleaning by drone

 Walking on an old tile roof or a fragile solar array is how roofs get broken and people get hurt. A drone treats and rinses from above, the team stays on the ground, and nothing is stepped on.

 Request a site survey 
 Become a pilot site 

## Roofs: treat the roots, not just the surface

 Moss, lichen and black algae hold water against tiles and metal, block gutters and age the roof. High-pressure washing removes what you see but damages tiles and leaves the roots, so it all grows back.

 We work the other way. The drone sprays a slow-acting biocide or enzymatic treatment over the whole roof. The product keeps working for weeks, and rain rinses away the dead growth. When the client wants an immediate result, we follow with a low-pressure rinse.

 Clay and concrete tiles, slate, metal sheet and standing seam

 Gutters, canopies, porches and covered walkways

 Treatment chosen for the material and the surroundings, applied according to the label

 No one on the roof, no broken tiles

## Solar panels: dust costs production

 Dust, pollen, bird droppings and soot settle on panels and cut the light reaching the cells. Panels on low-pitch roofs and carports do not self-clean well in the rain, and walking on them can crack cells or void warranties.

 Our drone cleans with purified water at low pressure, without detergent and without contact. It works over large arrays on warehouse and factory roofs, carport canopies and hotel roofs, and it never puts weight on the modules.

 Thailand has a growing number of rooftop installations on industrial buildings. For many of them, a drone is the only way to clean without scaffolding or roof walkways. We plan cleaning early in the morning when panels are cool.

## On our French job sites
 Roof jobs in the Paris region: moss treatment on old tile roofs and cleaning of metal roofs and solar canopies.

## Typical Thai sites

### Factories and warehouses 
 Large metal roofs and rooftop solar arrays on industrial estates, cleaned without stopping production.

### Hotels and resorts
 Tiled and pitched roofs on villas and pavilions, where algae grows fast in shade and humidity.

### Carports and canopies
 Solar carports at malls, hospitals and offices, cleaned early in the morning before the car park fills up.

## Roof and solar questions

 Is the roof treatment safe for gardens and pools?

 We choose the product for the site and keep a margin around pools, water tanks and planted areas. Products are used according to their label and we protect sensitive areas before spraying.

 How long before the roof looks clean?

 With a slow-acting treatment, the moss dies within days and the roof clears progressively with the rain over the following weeks. A low-pressure rinse gives an immediate result if you need one.

 Do you use detergent on solar panels?

 No. Purified water at low pressure, and no contact with the modules. Check your panel manufacturer's cleaning guidelines; we follow them.

## RATP: 400 m² of glazing in one night

 The Paris transport operator needed glazing above its tracks cleaned without stopping trains. With its usual method, the same work would have taken several nights.

 CleanAlta cleaned 400 m² of glass in a single night, with no interruption to traffic. RATP reports that intervention time was divided by five.

 Saint-Gobain Recherche Aubervilliers Drone + pole Recurring contract 

## Saint-Gobain Recherche: from a test to a contract

 Saint-Gobain's research centre near Paris has large glazed façades over several floors. We combined a tethered drone for the upper levels and a water-fed pole for the lower ones and the entrance.

 Heated osmosed water, no detergent. After the first job, Saint-Gobain Recherche signed a contract for two cleaning passes a year.

 Read the Saint-Gobain case study → 

 AP-HP Hôpital européen Georges-Pompidou Paris 15e 2026 

## AP-HP: a working hospital, cleaned from its own helipad

 Hôpital européen Georges-Pompidou, part of Assistance Publique – Hôpitaux de Paris, has glazed stair towers and façades over several floors, with patients and staff inside at all times.

 Flying a 24 kg drone over a Paris hospital requires the approval of the Paris Police Prefecture. CleanAlta obtained it, and the drone took off from the hospital helipad, tethered to its ground unit. Nobody worked at height during spraying. The contract covers 8,570 m² of glazing.

# Thailand pilot program: be among the first sites cleaned by drone

 We are choosing a small number of buildings in Thailand for our first jobs. Pilot sites get a full method statement, Thai permits and insurance handled by us, a documented before-and-after, and a tailored price. In return, we ask to document and publish the result.

 Apply as a pilot site 
 Ask a question 

## The sites we are looking for

 We want buildings where a drone makes a real difference, and owners or managers who are curious enough to try a new method.

### Hotels and resorts
 Glass façades, atriums, pool buildings, villa roofs. Bangkok, Phuket, Pattaya, Koh Samui, Chiang Mai.

### Condos and office towers
 Curtain walls where gondolas are slow, missing on some façades, or due for replacement.

### Hospitals and universities
 Sites that never close and need cleaning without workers at height outside rooms.

### Factories and warehouses
 Large roofs and rooftop solar arrays on industrial estates in the Eastern Economic Corridor and around Bangkok.

## What a pilot site gets

 A site survey and a written method statement for your building

 Drone and operator registration with the NBTC and the CAAT, and the flight permissions your site requires

 Third-party liability insurance covering the job

 A crew trained on French job sites, with the method used for RATP and Saint-Gobain

 A before-and-after report with photos and surfaces cleaned

 A tailored price, and priority when we set up regular service

## What we ask in return

 Access to the site, a take-off area, water and power

 A contact on site who can close access below the work zone

 Permission to film and photograph the job

 Permission to publish the result as a reference, anonymised if you prefer

 Honest feedback after the job

 We will only start flights in Thailand once registrations, permissions and insurance are in place. If a site cannot be authorised, we will say so and not fly.

## How it works

### Apply
 Fill in the form or send an email with the address, building type, height and a few photos.

### Remote assessment
 We review photos, maps and airspace around your site and tell you whether drone cleaning is possible and useful.

### Site visit
 We visit with our local partner, check take-off areas, obstacles, wind, water and power, and agree the schedule.

### Permits and insurance
 Registrations and permissions with the Thai authorities, insurance certificate, method statement shared with your team.

### Cleaning day
 Perimeter set up, test area, cleaning by drone and pole, final rinse. The duration is set in the method statement.

### Report and next steps
 Photos, surfaces, observations, and a proposal for regular cleaning if you want it.

## Why we are coming to Thailand

 Thailand combines tall glazed buildings, a climate that dirties façades fast, a huge hospitality sector and a fast-growing base of rooftop solar on industrial buildings. The Department of Tourism counted 17,126 hotels and 711,729 rooms in the first half of 2024.

 Thai rules on drones are clear and enforced: registration, insurance, distances from people, permissions for urban flights. That suits a company like ours, used to working under French and EU rules with prefecture authorisations.

 We would rather start small and do it properly than announce a network of cities. The first regions will be the ones where our pilot sites are.

 17,126 hotels in Thailand, H1 2024 

 711,729 hotel rooms, H1 2024 

 1M THB minimum third-party insurance for drones 

 2 years validity of CAAT registration 

## Pilot program questions

 Is the pilot free?

 No, but it is priced to make trying the method easy. The price depends on the building and is set after the site survey.

 When will the first jobs take place?

 As soon as we have selected sites, confirmed our local partner and obtained registrations and permissions. We will give each applicant a realistic date after the remote assessment.

 Which cities do you cover?

 We will start where the pilot sites are. Applications from Bangkok, the Eastern Seaboard, Phuket, Koh Samui and Chiang Mai are all welcome.

 Who will be on site?

 A CleanAlta pilot trained in France and our Thai partner's team. All flights follow the Thai rules for drone operations.

# Strategic partnership and investment in Thailand

 CleanAlta built its drone façade-cleaning method on demanding French sites: a railway station at night, a research centre, a working hospital. We are selecting one strategic partner and a small number of investors to launch the activity in Thailand.

 Request the investor brief

## Who we want to work with

Safety & compliance 

# Safety and compliance: Thai drone rules, and how we apply them

 Cleaning a building by drone means flying a heavy aircraft close to a façade, often in a city. In France we do it under EU rules with prefecture authorisations. In Thailand we will do it under CAAT and NBTC rules. This page sums up what the law requires and what we do on top.

## What Thai rules require

 The summary below is based on the Thai government's public guidance on drone registration and flight rules, dated 27 June 2025. Rules change and temporary restrictions apply in some areas, so we check current CAAT notices before every job.

 Topic Requirement 

 Registration Drone registered with the NBTC (radio equipment), then drone and operator registered with the CAAT through the UAS Portal. Registration is valid for two years. 

 Insurance Third-party liability insurance of at least 1,000,000 THB. 

 Visibility Daylight flights only, with the drone in visual line of sight. 

 Height Special approval needed above 90 metres. 

 Airports No flight within 9 km of an airport without authorisation. 

 Distance from people For drones of 2 to 25 kg, keep 50 metres from people not involved in the operation. 

 Urban areas and gatherings Flights over cities, crowds and gatherings require permission. Special operations are handled by the CAAT UAS unit. 

 Sources: Thai government portal thailand.go.th (27 June 2025); CAAT UAS unit. Temporary restrictions, such as those announced near some border zones in November 2025, show that local rules can change at short notice.

## What this means for a cleaning job

 A façade cleaning drone is in the 2 to 25 kg class and works close to buildings, usually in a city. In practice, every job needs registered equipment and pilots, insurance, and a specific permission for the site. The 50-metre rule means we close and control the ground area below the work zone, and we plan work at times when the area is quiet.

 A tethered drone helps: it is held by its cable and hose, so it cannot drift away, and its power comes from the ground. That does not replace any permission, but it makes the safety case clearer for the authorities and for building owners.

## Our status today

 CleanAlta has not yet registered drones or pilots in Thailand. Registrations, insurance and permissions will be completed with our Thai partner before the first pilot job. We will not fly before that.

## How we work in France

 In France, CleanAlta's flights are carried out under the EU “specific” category, including the STS-01 standard scenario, with prefecture authorisations for urban sites. TELEPILOTE SAS, the drone training centre founded in 2014, acts as UAS operator for these flights. We have obtained authorisations for sensitive urban sites in Paris, including hospitals.

## Our safety rules on every site

 Written method statement shared with the site before the job

 Closed and marked perimeter below the work zone, with a ground operator in charge

 Test flight and test area before cleaning

 Wind and rain limits: we stop when conditions are outside the drone's limits

 Pre-flight checklist on drone, tether, hose and ground unit

 Coordination with the building's security and facility teams

## Water and products

 On glass we use only purified water. On roofs, we use slow-acting biocide or enzymatic products, chosen for the surface and applied according to the label, with protection of pools, water tanks and planted areas. We bring our own water treatment unit.

## Compliance questions

 Who is responsible if something goes wrong?

 The registered operator, who must hold third-party liability insurance. For each job we provide the insurance certificate and the method statement before work starts.

 Can you fly near a hospital or an airport?

 Only with the right permission. Near airports, the 9 km rule applies. In France we have flown on hospital sites with prefecture authorisation; in Thailand the same kind of approval will be requested from the CAAT.

 Do you need to close the street?

 Not always. We need a controlled area under the drone. Depending on the building, that can be a courtyard, a car park section or a pavement closed for a few hours, agreed with the site.

About us 

# About CleanAlta

 CleanAlta is a French building cleaning company that works at height without putting people at height. We use tethered drones, water-fed poles and aerial platforms, and we pick the tool for the façade, not the other way round.

## The story

 Vincent Goleau has flown drones professionally for more than ten years. In 2014 he founded TELEPILOTE, a training centre for professional drone pilots in France. CleanAlta started from a simple observation: cleaning glass and façades at height is slow, expensive and dangerous for the people doing it, and drones could change that.

 In December 2024 he founded CleanAlta SAS to answer that problem with a method, not a gadget. The first jobs were for demanding clients: RATP, Saint-Gobain Recherche, CNRS, CHU de Toulouse. Each one taught us something and became a protocol.

 Our signature in France is “L'humain d'abord”: people first. The drone is a means. What matters is that nobody gets hurt, the building is clean, and the site keeps running.

## Leadership

 Vincent Goleau has flown drones professionally for more than ten years, among the first in France. He founded TELEPILOTE in 2014, a training centre whose instructors have accumulated more than 40,000 flight hours, and CleanAlta SAS in December 2024.

 His line on the method: the drone is a means. What matters is that nobody gets hurt, the building is clean, and the site keeps running. “L'humain d'abord”: people first.

 CleanAlta on LinkedIn · About page on cleanalta.com (French)

 We are in an opportunity phase: we are looking for pilot sites and a Thai partner, and we will grow from there. No promises of nationwide coverage, no invented case studies.

FAQ 

# Drone building cleaning in Thailand: the questions people ask us

 Short answers, written by the people who do the work. Where a figure comes from a real job or a published rule, we say so. Where we do not know yet, we say that too.

## Cost and speed

 How much does drone façade cleaning cost in Thailand?

 We do not publish a price per square metre, because the price depends on height, access, surface type, dirt level and how often you clean. We quote after a site survey. For the first Thai sites, the pilot program offers a tailored price in exchange for documenting the job. As a rule, drone cleaning is competitive against rope access and gondola work as soon as the building is tall, large or hard to access, because there is no scaffolding, no anchors and far fewer hours at height.

 How fast is it?

 500 to 800 m² per hour on suitable surfaces, depending on dirt level, method and protocol. This is the rate we use on French jobs. Set-up, safety perimeter and finishing with the pole or platform come on top. For reference, RATP reports that our night job at Paris Saint-Lazare cut intervention time by five compared with its usual method.

 How often should a building be cleaned in Thailand?

 More often than in Europe. Humidity, heat, dust, traffic and sea air dirty façades fast. Hotels and offices typically want glass cleaned two to four times a year. We recommend a schedule after the first job, once we have seen how fast your building gets dirty.

 Is there a minimum job size?

 Not a fixed one. Mobilising a drone team makes sense from a few hundred square metres upwards, or for smaller surfaces that are very hard to reach. Below that, a water-fed pole is often the right tool and we will say so.

## Legal and safety

 Is drone cleaning legal in Thailand?

 Yes, within a framework. Drones must be registered with the NBTC and with the CAAT through the UAS Portal, the operator needs third-party liability insurance of at least 1,000,000 THB, flights are in daylight within visual line of sight, special approval is needed above 90 m, within 9 km of an airport, and over cities or gatherings. Our summary and sources are on the compliance page .

 Is CleanAlta registered in Thailand today?

 No. We are selecting pilot sites and a local partner. Drones, pilots, insurance and permissions will be in place before the first Thai job. We will not fly before that.

 What happens if the drone fails in flight?

 The drone is tethered: its cable and hose hold it, and its power comes from the ground, so it cannot fly away or run out of battery. The ground under the work zone is closed and controlled during the whole job. In France we fly under EU rules with prefecture authorisations on sensitive urban sites, including hospitals.

 Who is on the ground during a job?

 A pilot, a ground operator who manages the hose, the tether and the perimeter, and a pole or platform operator when needed. Nobody works at height during application.

 Do you need to close the street?

 Not always. We need a controlled area under the drone: a courtyard, a section of car park or a pavement closed for a few hours. We agree it with the site and, when required, with the authorities.

## Method and products

 What water do you use?

 Osmosed water, heated, at low pressure. Reverse osmosis removes the minerals that leave white marks when tap water dries. Heat lifts grease and pollution. We bring our own treatment unit and connect to a water point on site.

 Do you use detergent or chemicals?

 Not on glass. On roofs, we apply slow-acting biocide or enzymatic treatments against moss and algae, chosen for the surface and used according to the label, with protection of pools, tanks and plants.

 Will it leave streaks on the windows?

 No. Streaks come from minerals in tap water and from detergent residues. We use neither on glass.

 Can the drone damage the façade?

 The drone never touches the building. It sprays at low pressure from a short distance. On sensitive materials we test a small area first and adjust temperature, distance and passes. In France we have written protocols per material: limestone, flamed stoneware, concrete, lacquered steel, glass.

 What does the drone not do well?

 Heavy encrusted dirt that needs brushing, very narrow spaces, and detail work on frames and joints. For those we use the water-fed pole or the aerial platform in the same visit. We also do not fly in strong wind or rain.

## Buildings and weather

 Which buildings are a good fit?

 Buildings from about four floors up with large glass or cladding surfaces, curved façades, atriums, closed courtyards, and roofs or solar arrays that are hard to reach. See the pages for hotels , condominiums and offices , hospitals and universities and factories and solar .

 Can you work while the building is occupied?

 Yes. In France we clean hospitals, research centres and stations while they stay open, sometimes at night. We agree the schedule and the perimeter with the facility team.

 What about the monsoon?

 We do not fly in rain or strong wind. In Thailand we plan jobs in the dry season where possible and keep flexible dates during the rainy months. Early mornings are usually the calmest.

 Can you clean solar panels on a factory roof?

 Yes, with purified water, no detergent and no contact with the modules. We never put weight on the panels and we follow the panel manufacturer's cleaning guidelines.

 Do you also inspect buildings or make 3D models?

 No. The Thai offer is cleaning only. If you need inspection, thermography or 3D modelling, we can point you to specialised operators.

## About CleanAlta

 Who is CleanAlta?

 A French building cleaning company founded in December 2024 by Vincent Goleau, a professional drone pilot for more than ten years. We work in France and Switzerland for clients such as RATP, Saint-Gobain Recherche, CNRS and CHU de Toulouse. More on the about page .

 Do you have references in Thailand?

 Not yet, and we will not invent any. Our references are French and public. The first Thai pilot sites will be published here once done.

 Which cities do you cover in Thailand?

 We will start where the pilot sites are. Applications from Bangkok , Pattaya and the Eastern Seaboard , Phuket , Koh Samui and Chiang Mai are welcome.

 Can I talk to one of your clients?

 Yes, for serious projects, with the client's agreement.

 How do I get a quote?

 Send photos, the address and the building height through the contact page . We answer with a first opinion, then a site visit before any price.

URL: https://dronecleaningthailand.com/en/drone-vs-rope-access-gondola/
Comparison 

# Drone, rope access, gondola, platform or pole: which one for your building?

 There is no single best way to clean a façade. We use three of the five methods below ourselves and we say no to the drone when another tool does the job better. Here is how we choose.

 Short answer: a tethered drone is the fastest option on large, tall, flat or curved surfaces with a clear ground area below, and it keeps everyone on the ground. Rope access remains the right choice for detail work on complex façades. A building maintenance unit (gondola) is efficient where it exists and reaches every façade. A water-fed pole wins below about 17 m. An aerial platform is for detail work and places the drone cannot fly close to. Most of our jobs combine two methods.

 Method Best for Speed People at height Main limits 

 Tethered drone Large glass and cladding surfaces, curved façades, inner courtyards, roofs, solar arrays 500–800 m²/h on suitable surfaces None during application Wind, rain, permits, ground perimeter, encrusted dirt needing a brush 

 Rope access Detail work, complex façades, inspections by hand Slow on large surfaces Yes, technicians on ropes Anchors needed on the roof, weather, working-at-height risk, workers in front of rooms 

 Gondola (BMU) Towers that already have one, regular glass cleaning Medium Yes, in the cradle Only where installed, maintenance and downtime, does not reach every façade or canopy 

 Aerial platform Detail work, frames and joints, low and medium heights Medium to slow Yes, in the basket Needs ground access and space, up to about 40 m, slow on very large surfaces 

 Water-fed pole Ground to fourth floor, shop fronts, glass roofs over lift shafts, canopies Fast at low height None Height, about 17 m maximum 

## Where the drone wins

 Tall buildings without a gondola , or with a gondola that does not reach every façade.

 Curved, stepped or set-back façades that a cradle or platform cannot follow.

 Closed courtyards and atriums where nothing with wheels can get in.

 Occupied buildings : no worker hanging outside guest rooms, patient rooms or offices.

 Fragile roofs and solar arrays that must not be walked on.

 Short interventions : set-up in hours, not days of scaffolding.

 Curved façade: the drone follows the shape, a platform cannot

## Where the drone loses

 Heavy encrusted dirt that needs mechanical brushing: the pole or the platform does it.

 Frames, joints, sills, detail work : a person with a brush is better.

 Wind and rain : the drone stays on the ground.

 No safe ground area below the work zone: we cannot close a perimeter, we do not fly.

 Airport zones and restricted airspace without permission.

 That is why our teams carry a 17 m carbon pole and can bring a 40 m platform. The drone does the volume, the pole and the platform do the finish.

## What drives the cost
 Whatever the method, five things set the price.

### Access and set-up
 Scaffolding and anchors cost days. A gondola costs maintenance. A drone needs a perimeter and permits. The pole needs nothing.

### Hours at height
 Every hour with a person on a rope or in a basket is slower and more supervised than an hour with a pilot on the ground.

### Surface and dirt
 Glass with pollution film is fast. Textured cladding with algae is slow. Encrusted dirt needs brushing whatever the tool.

### Frequency
 A building cleaned three times a year is cheaper per pass than one cleaned every three years.

### Disruption
 Closing a car park for a morning is cheap. Closing a hotel wing for a week is not. Night work costs more per hour but saves days.

### Site constraints
 Water and power on site, take-off area, airspace. We check all of this in the survey before quoting.

## Comparison questions

 Is drone cleaning cheaper than rope access?

 Usually, on large surfaces: fewer hours, no anchors, no days of set-up. On small or detailed surfaces, rope access or a pole can be cheaper. We quote both when it is close.

 Is drone cleaning safer?

 Nobody works at height during application, and the ground zone is closed and controlled, with a prevention plan. The risk moves from people to equipment, which is why the drone is tethered and why we follow the Thai distance and permit rules.

 Can a drone replace our building maintenance unit?

 It can replace it for cleaning the surfaces the gondola reaches, and add the ones it does not. It does not replace it for glass replacement or maintenance tasks.

 Can the drone clean windows from the inside?

 No. Interior glass is done by hand or with a pole.

# Where we work in Thailand

 Honest version: nowhere yet. We are selecting the first pilot sites, and the first regions we serve will be the ones where those sites are. The five areas below are where the buildings, the climate and the demand make drone cleaning most useful, and where we are actively looking.

 Capital

 Glass towers, condominiums, hospitals, malls. The densest building stock in the country and the most complex airspace, with two airports.

## How we will choose the first regions

 Three things decide where we start: a client ready to be a pilot site, a local partner with a team to train, and airspace where permits are realistic. A hotel in Phuket with a clear beach-side take-off area is easier to authorise than a tower next to an airport.

 Thai rules keep drones 9 km from airports without permission, 50 m from people not involved in the operation for drones between 2 and 25 kg, and require specific permission for urban flights. Each city page below says what that means in practice. Details and sources are on the compliance page .

 Thailand's hotel stock alone is large: 17,126 hotels and 711,729 rooms in the first half of 2024 according to the Department of Tourism. Add condominiums, offices, hospitals, universities, malls and factories, and the question is not whether there is work, but where to do the first jobs well.

 Source: Department of Tourism, H1 2024, quoted in LH Bank, Industry Outlook 2025.

Bangkok · Pilot sites wanted 

# Drone façade and window cleaning in Bangkok

 Bangkok has more glass towers, condominiums, hospitals and malls than any other Thai city, and the dirtiest air to go with them. It is also the most regulated airspace in the country. We are looking for two or three Bangkok buildings to run our first documented jobs, with permits handled properly.

 Apply as a Bangkok pilot site 
 Investors & partners 

## Why Bangkok façades get dirty so fast

 Traffic soot, construction dust, humidity above 70% most of the year and a long rainy season leave a grey film on glass and a black streak under every sill. Dark algae grows on north-facing and shaded walls. Buildings along the expressways and the Chao Phraya get it worst.

 Most towers were built with a gondola, but many gondolas are ageing, booked, or do not reach set-backs, podiums, canopies and atriums. Rope access fills the gap, with technicians hanging outside offices and condo units for days.

 A tethered drone cleans the same glass from a short distance, at 500 to 800 m² per hour on suitable surfaces, with the pilot on the ground and nobody at height during application. For podiums, canopies and inner courtyards, it is often the only tool that fits.

## Bangkok buildings we are looking for

### Office towers and condominiums
 Sukhumvit, Sathorn, Silom, Rama 9, Ratchada: curtain walls where the gondola is slow or missing on a façade. See condominiums and offices .

### Hotels
 Riverside and city hotels with glass atriums, pool decks and canopies, cleaned early in the morning without workers outside guest rooms. See hotels .

### Hospitals and universities
 Large campuses that never close, where our hospital references in France are directly relevant. See hospitals .

### Malls and public buildings
 Glass roofs, canopies and entrance halls that nobody can reach from inside.

## Airspace and permits in Bangkok

 Bangkok has two airports, Suvarnabhumi to the east and Don Mueang to the north. Thai rules require permission to fly within 9 km of an airport, and urban flights need authorisation in any case. In practice, every Bangkok job needs a specific permission from the CAAT, and sites close to either airport need more lead time. We check the location of your building against these zones in the remote assessment, before anyone travels.

 The 50 m rule for drones between 2 and 25 kg means we need a controlled ground area under the work zone: a service yard, a section of car park, a closed drop-off lane. Dense sites can still work, with early-morning or night slots agreed with the building.

 CleanAlta has not yet registered drones or pilots in Thailand. Registrations, insurance and permissions will be done with our local partner before the first Bangkok job. Sources and details: compliance page .

## What a Bangkok pilot job would look like

### Remote assessment
 Photos, address, height. We check airspace, take-off options and surfaces, and say whether it is realistic.

### Site visit with our partner
 Water and power points, perimeter, timing with building management, security briefing.

### Permits and insurance
 CAAT permission for the site, NBTC and CAAT registrations, insurance certificate, method statement shared with your team.

### Job and report
 Test area, drone on the volume, pole on the details, before-and-after photos. Then a proposal for a yearly schedule.

## Bangkok questions

 Do you already have a team in Bangkok?
 Not yet. We are choosing a local partner and training will follow. The first jobs will be run by a CleanAlta pilot from France with the partner's team.

 Can you fly near Suvarnabhumi or Don Mueang?
 Only with CAAT permission, and with more lead time. Tell us the address and we will say quickly whether it is realistic.

 Can you work at night in Bangkok?
 Thai rules allow daylight flights only, unless a special permission is granted. In France we have done night jobs for RATP; in Thailand we will plan early mornings unless a permission allows otherwise.

 How do I apply?
 Through the pilot program or through the contact page with photos and the address.

# Drone cleaning for resorts, villas and condominiums in Phuket

 Sea air, humidity, heavy rain from May to October and strong sun the rest of the year: Phuket buildings fight salt, algae and dust all year. Resorts clean constantly, and most of them still do it with ladders, ropes and scaffolding on properties full of guests.

 Apply as a Phuket pilot site 
 Investors & partners 

## What the drone changes for a resort

 A resort is a collection of difficult surfaces: glass lobbies and restaurants, villa roofs in tile or thatch-look material, pool buildings, spa pavilions, covered walkways, and often a hillside layout where nothing with wheels can go. Cleaning it means weeks of people on ladders and ropes in front of guests.

 With a tethered drone, the team arrives in a van, sets up a perimeter around one building at a time, and cleans glass and roofs from the ground. Guests see a drone for a few hours, not scaffolding for a week. Early-morning slots fit before breakfast service.

 Glass façades, lobbies, restaurants and sea-view windows, rinsed with purified water, no streaks

 Roofs of villas and pavilions: algae and moss treatment, nobody walking on tiles

 Solar canopies and roof arrays on back-of-house buildings

 Rendered and painted walls stained by algae on the shaded side

## Phuket airspace and sites

 Phuket International Airport sits in the north of the island, near Mai Khao and Nai Yang. Thai rules require permission to fly within 9 km of an airport, so resorts on the north-west beaches need that permission and more lead time. Patong, Kata, Karon, Rawai, Cape Panwa and Phuket Town are outside that circle but still need the standard permissions for flights near people and buildings.

 Wind matters more than in Bangkok. We plan sea-facing façades in the morning and stop when the breeze picks up. The dry season from November to April is the natural window for large jobs.

 We have not flown in Phuket yet. Registrations, insurance and permissions will be in place before the first job. Details on the compliance page .

## Who we want to meet in Phuket

### Resort engineering managers
 You know which façades and roofs cost you the most each year. One pilot job on one building, documented, is how we start.

### Condominium juristic persons and managers
 Sea-view condos in Patong, Kata, Surin and Bang Tao with glass balconies and painted walls that need cleaning every year.

### Villa estate managers
 Estates of ten to a hundred villas, where one visit can cover many roofs in a few days.

## Phuket questions

 Can you clean a resort while it is full?
 Yes. We work building by building, early in the morning, with a closed perimeter. In France we clean hospitals and stations while they operate.

 Does salt need a special treatment?
 Salt dissolves in water. Heated purified water removes it without detergent. The issue is frequency: sea-facing glass needs more passes per year than city glass.

 What about thatch or shingle roofs?
 We assess them case by case. Low pressure and a slow-acting treatment work on most, but we test a small area first and we will say no if the material cannot take water.

Eastern Seaboard · Pilot sites wanted 

# Drone cleaning in Pattaya, Chonburi and the Eastern Economic Corridor

 Two very different jobs in one region: the industrial estates of Chonburi and Rayong, with their metal roofs and rooftop solar, and the seafront hotels and condominiums of Pattaya and Jomtien. The drone is useful for both, for different reasons.

 Apply as a pilot site 
 Investors & partners 

## Factories, warehouses and rooftop solar

 The industrial estates between Laem Chabang, Si Racha, Amata and Map Ta Phut hold thousands of large metal roofs, and a growing number of them carry solar panels. Dust from traffic and production, bird droppings and algae settle on both. Panels lose output, roofs stain and gutters block.

 Cleaning them by hand means roof walkways, harness lines, and people on fragile sheets or on panels that must not be stepped on. A tethered drone cleans a metal roof or a PV array from above, with purified water and no contact, and the operator stays on the ground. Production does not stop.

 Metal sheet and standing-seam roofs, skylights, gutters

 Rooftop PV arrays and solar carports, no detergent, no weight on modules

 Cladding and façades of logistics buildings and showrooms

 Early-morning slots when panels are cool and car parks are empty

 Metal roof of an industrial building cleaned by drone

## Pattaya and Jomtien: seafront glass

 Pattaya's hotels and condominium towers face the sea and the wind. Salt and sand stick to glass balconies and curtain walls, and the shaded sides go green with algae. Gondolas are rare on older towers, and rope access teams spend days in front of occupied rooms.

 A drone cleans a seafront façade in a few hours from a closed section of the pool deck or car park, before guests come down. For buildings with a gondola, the drone adds the surfaces the cradle does not reach: podiums, canopies, set-backs.

## Airspace on the Eastern Seaboard

 U-Tapao airport lies between Pattaya and Rayong, and the 9 km rule applies around it. Most of Pattaya itself, Si Racha, Laem Chabang and the Amata estates are outside that circle, but industrial estates often have their own restrictions and security rules, and flights near people and buildings still need the standard permissions. We check each address in the remote assessment.

 We have not flown on the Eastern Seaboard yet. Registrations, insurance and permissions will be in place before the first job. Details on the compliance page .

## Eastern Seaboard questions

 Can you clean solar panels while the plant is running?
 Yes. Purified water, low pressure, no contact. We follow the panel manufacturer's cleaning guidelines and work early in the morning when modules are cool.

 Do you need to enter the factory?
 We need a take-off area, a water point and a power supply, usually in a yard or car park. We follow the site's safety induction and permit-to-work process.

 How big a roof can you do in a day?
 On suitable surfaces, 500 to 800 m² per hour. A full day on a large roof is realistic, weather allowing. Set-up and moves between buildings come on top.

Koh Samui · Pilot sites wanted 

# Drone cleaning for hillside villas and resorts on Koh Samui

 Samui's best properties sit on steep hills above Chaweng, Lamai, Bophut and Taling Ngam, with sea views, glass walls and roofs that no aerial platform can reach. Cleaning them means ladders, ropes and risk. A tethered drone arrives in a van and works from the terrace.

 Apply as a Samui pilot site 
 Investors & partners 

## Why hillside properties are a drone job

 On a hillside, access is the whole problem. Roads are narrow, driveways steep, and a 40 m platform cannot get near the building. Scaffolding has to be carried by hand. So roofs go green, glass goes grey, and cleaning happens less often than it should.

 A tethered drone needs a few square metres of flat ground, a water point and a power supply or our generator. From a terrace or a pool deck it reaches the roof, the glass walls and the rendered façades of a villa in a morning, then moves to the next one.

 Tiled and shingle roofs: slow-acting algae and moss treatment, nobody on the roof

 Floor-to-ceiling glass and sea-view windows, purified water, no streaks

 Rendered and painted walls with algae on the shaded side

 Resort pavilions, spa roofs, covered walkways and pool buildings

 Moss treatment on an old tiled roof by drone

## Samui airspace and weather

 Samui Airport is on the north-east of the island, between Bophut and Chaweng. The 9 km rule covers a large part of the north-east coast, including Chaweng, Bophut and Choeng Mon, so properties there need CAAT permission and more lead time. The west and south of the island are outside that circle, with the standard permissions still required.

 Rain peaks in October and November on Samui. The best window for large jobs runs from January to August, with early-morning slots to avoid the afternoon breeze.

 We have not flown on Samui yet. Registrations, insurance and permissions will be in place before the first job. Details on the compliance page .

## Samui questions

 Can one visit cover several villas?
 Yes, that is the point. An estate or a management company with ten or more villas is the ideal pilot: one mobilisation, many roofs.

 What do you need from the villa?
 A few square metres of flat ground, a garden tap, a socket or space for our generator, and someone to keep guests and staff out of the zone below the drone for a few hours.

 Do you treat moss or just rinse it?
 We treat it. A slow-acting product keeps working for weeks and the rain clears the dead growth. Rinsing alone brings it back within months in Samui's climate.

Chiang Mai · Pilot sites wanted 

# Drone façade and glass cleaning in Chiang Mai

 Chiang Mai has a dust and smoke season from February to April that coats every window in the city, then a rainy season that turns the film into streaks. Hotels, universities, hospitals and the new condominium towers along the Ping river all clean glass more often than they would like.

 Apply as a Chiang Mai pilot site 
 Investors & partners 

## The right buildings in Chiang Mai

 Chiang Mai is lower-rise than Bangkok, which is good news for drone work: most buildings are between four and fifteen floors, few have gondolas, and many have courtyards, canopies and glass roofs. These are the surfaces where a tethered drone replaces days of scaffolding.

 Hotels and boutique resorts in Nimman, the old city and along the river, cleaned before breakfast service

 University and hospital campuses with large glass buildings that stay open all year

 Condominium towers with glass balconies and painted walls

 Malls and showrooms with glass roofs and canopies

 After the smoke season, a single pass with heated purified water removes the grey film without detergent. We recommend a second pass after the rains.

## Airspace in Chiang Mai

 Chiang Mai International Airport sits south-west of the old city, closer to the centre than any other major Thai airport. The 9 km rule therefore covers the old city, Nimman, the university area and most of the urban core. Every job in the city will need CAAT permission with that in mind, and lead times will be longer than elsewhere. Sites further out, towards Mae Rim, San Kamphaeng or Hang Dong, are easier.

 We will say in the remote assessment whether a given address is realistic, before anyone travels.

 We have not flown in Chiang Mai yet. Registrations, insurance and permissions will be in place before the first job. Details on the compliance page .

## Chiang Mai questions

 Is it realistic to fly inside the old city?
 Only with CAAT permission because of the airport. We will not promise a date before the permission is in hand.

 When is the best time of year?
 Right after the smoke season, in April and May, and again after the rains in November. Early mornings in the cool season are ideal for flying.

 Can you do a university campus in one visit?
 Large campuses are done building by building over several days, with a schedule agreed with the facility team. That is how we work on research centres in France.

Hotels · Resorts 

# Drone cleaning for hotels and resorts

 A hotel cannot close to be cleaned. Scaffolding in the lobby view, rope technicians outside the suites and a gondola rattling past the windows all cost guest satisfaction. A tethered drone cleans glass, façades and roofs from the ground, early in the morning, building by building.

 Apply as a pilot hotel 
 See photos and videos 

## The surfaces that cost hotels the most

### Glass façades and sea-view windows
 Salt, dust and rain streaks. Heated purified water at low pressure, rinsed without streaks and without detergent.

### Atriums, lobbies and glass roofs
 Surfaces nobody can reach from inside without a scissor lift in the lobby. The drone does them from outside.

### Villa and pavilion roofs
 Algae and moss on tiles in shaded, humid spots. Slow-acting treatment from above, nobody walking on the roof.

### Pool buildings and canopies
 Covered walkways, spa roofs, restaurant canopies: cleaned in a morning from the pool deck.

## How a hotel job runs

### Plan with the engineering manager
 Which buildings, which mornings, which areas to close for a few hours. We fit the schedule around occupancy and events.

### Perimeter, then flight
 Ground area closed under the work zone, guests informed, drone on the glass and the roof. Pole on the ground floor and the details.

### Report and schedule
 Before-and-after photos per building, then a yearly schedule: typically two to four passes on glass in Thailand's climate.

 In France, our clients include a working university hospital and a research centre that stayed open during the job. The discipline is the same for a hotel: a perimeter, a schedule, no surprises.

 Purified water jet on upper-floor windows

## Why hotels are our first target in Thailand

 Thailand counted 17,126 hotels and 711,729 rooms in the first half of 2024 (Department of Tourism, via LH Bank). Resorts clean constantly, they care about how work looks to guests, and many sit where scaffolding and platforms struggle: hillsides, beaches, islands. That is a drone job.

 We are looking for hotels in Phuket , Koh Samui , Bangkok , Pattaya and Chiang Mai willing to be among the first documented jobs. A pilot hotel gets a tailored price and priority when we set up regular service.

## Hotel questions

 Will guests be disturbed?
 They will see a drone for a few hours in the morning and a small closed area on the ground. No scaffolding, no one outside their window, no noise comparable to a gondola.

 Is the water safe around pools and gardens?
 On glass we use only purified water. On roofs, the treatment is chosen for the site, applied according to the label, and we keep a margin around pools, tanks and plants.

 Can you clean during high season?
 Yes, with early-morning slots. Many hotels prefer it, because the building looks its best when it is full.

 What does the hotel need to provide?
 A water point, a socket or space for our generator, a take-off area, and someone to keep the ground zone clear during the job.

# Drone glass cleaning for condominiums and office towers

 Most towers in Thailand have a building maintenance unit, and most of those units are slow, often out of service, or blind to podiums, set-backs and canopies. Rope access fills the gap with days of technicians outside units. A tethered drone cleans the same glass from the ground.

 Request a site survey 
 Drone vs gondola vs rope access 

## What managers ask for

 Fewer days of disruption : a façade in hours, not a week of ropes outside the units

 No complaints from residents : nobody at their window, no gondola at 7 am

 The surfaces the gondola misses : podium, canopies, set-backs, inner courtyards, glass roofs over lift shafts

 A clean result without streaks : purified water, no detergent, no wiping

 A written method statement and insurance before anyone starts

 A yearly schedule and a fixed price per pass 

 In France we clean curtain walls, inner courtyards and glass roofs for building owners and facility managers, including a glass structure above live railway tracks for RATP, done in one night with intervention time divided by five.

## For the juristic person or the facility manager

 1 
### One survey, one method statement
 We walk the building with you, note take-off areas, water and power, and write the plan: which façade by drone, which by pole, which by platform.

 2 
### Permits and insurance in your file
 CAAT permission for the site, registrations, insurance certificate. You get copies before the job for your board or your client.

 3 
### Report you can forward
 Before-and-after photos per façade, surfaces cleaned, observations on seals, cracked glass or corrosion we saw from close up.

## Towers with a gondola: drone as a complement

 If your building maintenance unit works well, keep it. The drone adds what it cannot do: podiums and canopies, set-back floors, courtyard façades, glass roofs, and a fast pass between gondola cycles. If the unit is out of service for months, which happens, the drone keeps the building clean without waiting.

 We are looking for office and condominium towers in Bangkok , Pattaya , Phuket and Chiang Mai for the first documented jobs.

 98 seconds at the Paris Conservatoire (CNSMDP), La Villette

## Condominium and office questions

 Do residents need to close their windows?
 Yes, during the pass on their façade. We give the building a schedule by façade and by morning so the juristic office can inform residents.

 Can you clean balconies and glass balustrades?
 The outside face, yes. Inside faces and balcony floors are not part of the drone job.

 What about a 40-storey tower?
 Thai rules require special approval above 90 m. Up to that height the drone works normally; above it, we request the approval or combine with the gondola.

 Can you quote a yearly contract?
 Yes. After the first job we propose a schedule with a price per pass, usually two to four passes a year for glass in Thailand.

# Drone cleaning for hospitals and universities

 A hospital never closes. Rope technicians outside patient rooms, a gondola in front of an operating theatre window, scaffolding at an emergency entrance: every option has a cost beyond money. In France we have cleaned the eighth-floor windows of a working university hospital in Toulouse, and the glazing of an AP-HP hospital in Paris with the drone taking off from the hospital helipad. Nobody at height during application. The same method is ready for Thailand.

 Talk to us about your campus 
 Our hospital and research references 

## References that matter here

 AP-HP · Hôpital européen Georges-Pompidou 
### A Paris hospital, cleaned from its helipad
 Glazed stair towers and façades of a working hospital. Flights approved by the Paris Police Prefecture, 24 kg tethered drone, nobody at height during spraying. Contract: 8,570 m² of glazing.

 CHU de Toulouse · Rangueil 
### Windows on the 8th floor of a working hospital
 Cleaned without closing services and with no one working at height during application. This is the closest case to a Thai hospital.

 Saint-Gobain Recherche 
### A research centre that stayed open
 Large glazed façades over several floors, cleaned by drone and pole while laboratories kept working. Led to a two-passes-a-year contract.

 CNRS · ISMO, Orsay 
### A university institute's glass façade
 The “periodic table” façade of coloured glass panels, cleaned with a drone and an aerial platform.

## How we work on a site that never closes

 Method statement and prevention plan written with the facility and security teams before the job

 Perimeter on the ground under the work zone, timed to avoid ambulance routes and shift changes

 Façade by façade , with wards informed of the morning their windows will be done

 No chemicals on glass : heated purified water only, nothing enters the ventilation

 Tethered drone : it cannot drift away, and its power comes from the ground

 Report with photos for the technical department and the board

 In France we have obtained prefecture authorisations for sensitive urban hospital sites. In Thailand, the equivalent will be a CAAT permission for the site, and hospitals near airports will need more lead time.

 Inside the van: water treatment, pump and ground unit

## Universities and campuses

 Campuses have what drones are made for: many mid-rise buildings, glass libraries and lecture halls, courtyards, covered walkways and a facility team that plans a year ahead. We work building by building over several days, between terms where possible, and we leave a schedule for the following years.

 We are looking for a hospital or a university in Bangkok or Chiang Mai as one of the first Thai pilot sites.

## Hospital and campus questions

 Is there any risk of water entering the building?
 We spray at low pressure, top-down, on closed windows, and we check seals in the test area first. Windows that cannot close are noted in the method statement and done by pole.

 Is the drone noisy?
 Less than a gondola or a platform engine, and it stays a few minutes per window band. Wards are informed in advance.

 Can you work around a helipad?
 Only with the hospital's flight coordination and the authority's permission. In France we have done it; in Thailand it will be part of the CAAT request.

 Do you have public procurement experience?
 Yes, in France, with public hospitals, a public transport operator and a national research body. We can provide the documents a Thai public buyer usually asks for.

# Drone cleaning for factories, warehouses and rooftop solar

 An industrial roof is big, fragile and full of things nobody should walk on: skylights, panels, old sheets. A tethered drone cleans roofs, PV arrays, gutters and cladding from above with purified water, while the plant keeps running and the crew stays on the ground.

 Request a site survey 
 Roof and solar service 

## What we clean on an industrial site

### Rooftop solar arrays
 Dust, pollen, bird droppings and soot cut output. Purified water, low pressure, no detergent, no contact, no weight on modules.

### Metal roofs and skylights
 Algae, dirt and rust streaks on sheet and standing-seam roofs. Skylights cleared so daylight comes back in.

### Gutters and downpipes
 Blocked gutters flood roofs in the monsoon. In France we have cleaned 20 gutters of 42 m and 40 downpipes on one industrial site.

### Cladding and showrooms
 Painted and composite cladding, glass showrooms and offices on the front of the plant.

## Why plant managers like it

 No roof access : no harness lines, no walkways, no fragile-roof risk

 No production stop : the team works from a yard or car park, early in the morning

 Permit-to-work friendly : method statement, perimeter, safety induction, one contact

 Output back on PV : clean panels produce more, and we clean before the panels get hot

 A report with photos of the roof condition you cannot see from the ground

 In France we work for Veolia and Bouygues sites among others, and we hold a roof and solar cleaning offer with slow-acting algae treatments chosen for the material.

 Metal roof of an industrial building

## Where in Thailand

 The industrial estates of the Eastern Economic Corridor , Chonburi, Rayong and Chachoengsao, hold the largest concentration of big roofs and rooftop solar in the country. Estates around Bangkok , Ayutthaya and Pathum Thani are next. We are looking for one or two industrial sites as pilot jobs, ideally with a rooftop PV array and a metal roof on the same site.

## Industrial questions

 Do you need the solar plant switched off?
 Usually not. We use purified water at low pressure and no contact. We follow the installer's and manufacturer's guidelines and the site's permit-to-work.

 How do you handle a 20,000 m² roof?
 In sections, over several days, at 500 to 800 m² per hour on suitable surfaces. We plan moves between take-off points with the site.

 What about the water?
 We bring the treatment unit and connect to a site water point. Purified water only on panels and glass; the treatment on roofs is chosen for the material and applied according to the label.

 Can you fly inside an industrial estate?
 With the estate's rules and the standard Thai permissions, yes. Sites within 9 km of U-Tapao or another airport need CAAT permission with more lead time.

URL: https://dronecleaningthailand.com/en/references/ratp-paris-saint-lazare/
Case study · Public transport · Night work 

# RATP, Paris Saint-Lazare: 400 m² of glazing cleaned by drone in one night

 Paris Saint-Lazare is one of the busiest stations in Europe. Its glass “lens” sits above live tracks and could not be cleaned without stopping trains or putting people at height. In October 2025, CleanAlta cleaned it by tethered drone, at night, in a single intervention.

 By Vincent Goleau , founder of CleanAlta, professional drone pilot since 2014 Published 31 October 2026 Reviewed for the Thai market 

 In short: 400 m² of glazing above the tracks of Paris Saint-Lazare, cleaned in one night by a tethered drone with heated purified water, with no interruption to train traffic and nobody at height. RATP reports that the intervention time was divided by five compared with its usual method.

 Client RATP 

 Site Paris Saint-Lazare station 

 Date October 2025 

 Surface 400 m² of glass 

 Duration One night 

 Time saved ÷5 (RATP figure) 

## The problem

 The glass structure above the station tracks collects dust from the trains, city soot and rain marks. Cleaning it with the usual method meant several nights of work with technicians at height, each requiring a traffic interruption window. For an operator that runs trains almost around the clock, every night of work is a cost on its own.

## What CleanAlta did

 We prepared the job with RATP’s station management and safety teams: ground perimeter, electrical safety near the catenary, timing between the last and first trains, and the authorisation to fly in central Paris. On the night, a tethered drone under 25 kg sprayed heated purified water at low pressure on the glass, fed from a ground unit. The pilot and the ground crew stayed at platform level the whole time.

 400 m² of glass were cleaned in a single night. No train was delayed, and no one worked at height during spraying.

## Why it matters for Thailand

 Bangkok has the same kind of building: BTS and MRT stations, airport terminals, shopping-mall glass roofs and atriums where closing the site for cleaning is not an option. The method used at Saint-Lazare transfers directly: night work, no traffic interruption, nobody at height, and a cleaning rate of 500 to 800 m² per hour on large glass surfaces.

## In the press

 Le Journal du Grand Paris RATP tests drone cleaning of the Saint-Lazare station glass “lens” 
 France 3 Paris Île-de-France The Saint-Lazare station “lens” cleaned with drones 
 Ville, Rail & Transports A drone to make the Saint-Lazare station “bubble” shine 

 RATP has since commissioned CleanAlta on other sites, including Marne-la-Vallée Chessy station. Photo on the references page: glazing cleaned by drone on another Paris site.

## Questions about this job

 How can a drone clean glass above live railway tracks?
 The drone is tethered to a ground unit that supplies power and water, so it cannot fly away, and it works at night between the last and first trains. The crew stays on the platforms; nobody climbs on the structure.

 What does “intervention time divided by five” mean?
 It is RATP’s own comparison between the single night needed by CleanAlta and the time its usual method would have required for the same 400 m² of glazing.

 Could the same be done at a BTS or MRT station in Bangkok?
 Technically yes: the method is identical. In Thailand it requires NBTC and CAAT registration, third-party insurance and a permit for the urban flight, which CleanAlta handles before any pilot job.

# AP-HP, Hôpital européen Georges-Pompidou: a working hospital cleaned from its own helipad

 Assistance Publique – Hôpitaux de Paris is the largest hospital group in Europe. Its Georges-Pompidou hospital in the 15th arrondissement has glazed stair towers and façades over several floors, with patients and staff inside at all times. CleanAlta cleans them by tethered drone.

 By Vincent Goleau , founder of CleanAlta, professional drone pilot since 2014 Published 31 October 2026 Reviewed for the Thai market 

 In short: CleanAlta holds a contract for 8,570 m² of glazing at Hôpital européen Georges-Pompidou (AP-HP). The 24 kg tethered drone takes off from the hospital helipad under an agreement with the Paris Police Prefecture. The hospital stays fully open, and nobody works at height during spraying.

 Contract 8,570 m² of glazing

 Take-off Hospital helipad

## The problem

 A hospital never closes. Rope technicians outside patient rooms, a gondola in front of an operating theatre window or scaffolding at an emergency entrance all have a cost beyond money. At Georges-Pompidou, the structural glass stair towers and the façades are exactly the kind of surface where every conventional method puts people at height in front of care units.

 Flying a 24 kg drone over a hospital in central Paris requires the approval of the Paris Police Prefecture. Many operators consider it out of reach. CleanAlta prepared the operational file, the risk assessment and the flight protocol, and obtained the agreement in summer 2026, with take-off from the hospital helipad.

 The drone is tethered to a ground unit that supplies power and heated purified water. It sprays the glass at low pressure, with no detergent, and rinses it so that it dries without streaks. # Saint-Gobain Recherche: from a first job to a two-passes-a-year contract

 Saint-Gobain is the world’s leading glass manufacturer. Its research centre near Paris has large glazed façades over several floors and laboratories that keep working during cleaning. After a first job, Saint-Gobain Recherche signed a contract for two cleaning passes a year.

 By Vincent Goleau , founder of CleanAlta, professional drone pilot since 2014 Published 31 October 2026 Reviewed for the Thai market 

 In short: tethered drone for the upper floors, water-fed pole for the lower floors and the entrance, heated purified water and no detergent. Laboratories stayed open. The first job convinced Saint-Gobain Recherche to sign a contract for two cleaning passes a year.

 Client Saint-Gobain Recherche 

 Site Research centre, Aubervilliers (Paris region) 

 Methods Drone + water-fed pole 

 Water Heated, osmosed, no detergent 

 Outcome Two passes a year 

## The problem

 Glass façades over several floors, offices and laboratories behind them, and a site that cannot stop for cleaning. A gondola would have been slow; rope access would have put technicians in front of the windows for days.

## What CleanAlta did

 We combined two methods. A tethered drone cleaned the upper floors, spraying heated purified water at low pressure and rinsing it. A 17 m carbon water-fed pole handled the lower floors and the entrance, where precision matters more than speed. Both use the same water, produced on site by the osmosis unit in the van, so the glass dries without streaks and without detergent.

## The result

 The first job was a test. The client measured the result, compared it with its previous contractor, and signed for two passes a year. For a cleaning company, a recurring contract with a glass manufacturer is the best possible reference on the quality of the result.

## Why it matters for Thailand

 Office campuses, research centres and factories with glazed office blocks are common in Bangkok, the EEC and the industrial estates. The combination of drone and pole is the one we would use there: fast on the upper floors, precise at ground level, and no interruption for the people working inside.

## Questions about this job

 Why no detergent?
 Heated osmosed water dissolves dirt and dries without leaving minerals, so there is nothing to rinse off and no residue on the glass. It is also safer for the people and plants below.

 Why two methods on one building?
 The drone is fastest on large upper surfaces; the pole is more precise near the ground and the entrance. Using both gives the best result for the lowest cost.
